investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC (SUFFICIENT). All retained evidence acquired via plain curl (raw HTTP, no WebFetch/AI-markdown conversion, real descriptive User-Agent). sources/porto.json's existing forum-maia entry was read first for context (not edited). Its own events_url, https://www.cm-maia.pt/institucional/agenda/evento/agenda-cultural_fim-de-semana-88, returned an HTTP 301 redirect to a path-corrected same-page URL (…/institucional/atualidade-e-participacao/agenda/evento/agenda-cultural_fim-de-semana-88), which is itself a single dated ('fim de semana' = 'weekend') listing, not the live listing root — exactly the stale/dated-page concern flagged in this task. The site's own homepage (https://www.cm-maia.pt) was fetched and grepped for its own agenda navigation links, which independently pointed at a genuinely different, general listing root: /institucional/atualidade-e-participacao/agenda/todos-os-eventos ('all events'). That page, and 4 further pages of its own pagination plus its final page (283), were retained, along with two full event detail pages sampled specifically because their titles indicate genuine live/recorded music content (Maia Blues Fest 2026, a 3-day international blues festival; 'Sons de Verão 2026', a recurring outdoor concert series at the Auditório Exterior do Fórum da Maia) rather than being chosen arbitrarily. Every page is fully server-rendered static HTML with complete content in the initial response — no JSON-LD, no RSS/ICS feed, and no client-side rendering were found or required anywhere. Each event detail page embeds a structured (non-JSON, var-tag based) 'addtocalendar' widget exposing atc_date_start/atc_date_end/atc_timezone/atc_title/atc_location/atc_organizer directly, plus separately labelled Local:/Preço:/Organização:(/Horário: on some pages) fields — independently cross-checked against each other and against a third field (meta content_date) on the same page, and against the listing page's own href for the same event. A dependency-free, no-network Node offline-proof script re-parsed every retained evidence file to mechanically re-derive every claim below, including the identity check, the redirect-vs-general-listing contrast, the full 5-page category-taxonomy scan (no music-specific tag found anywhere in the bounded sample), the archive-scope check (page 283 contains 2014-dated events), and a stable-identifier trap check proving wm:page_id/event_detail_<id> are NOT usable as a per-event id (both are identical across two genuinely distinct sampled events) — matching this project's own previously-documented Hot Clube ICS UID caution. Level 1 alone answered identity, platform classification, data-path discovery, and field assessment in full; Level 2/3 structural or browser escalation was not attempted because nothing about this static, server-rendered source suggested Level 1 was insufficient — the only genuinely open question this investigation could not mechanically resolve was a content-scope one (see decision below), not an acquisition-technique one.

probe_history.reason: Plain curl GETs (BandOnTheMap-SourceInvestigation/0.1 UA) of https://www.cm-maia.pt (homepage), the given sources/porto.json events_url (a 301 redirect to a path-corrected same single-weekend page), the independently-discovered general listing root (/institucional/atualidade-e-participacao/agenda/todos-os-eventos, plus 4 further pagination pages and its final page 283), and two sampled event detail pages (Maia Blues Fest 2026, Sons de Verão 2026) all returned complete, fully server-rendered HTML in the initial response — real event titles, dates (day+month+2-digit-year directly on every listing card), category tags, and, on detail pages, a structured addtocalendar widget (atc_date_start/atc_date_end/atc_timezone/atc_location/atc_organizer) plus separately labelled Local:/Preço:/Organização: fields, cross-confirmed against a second independent meta field (content_date) on the same page. No JSON-LD, RSS, or ICS was found, but none was needed: the plain static HTML itself already fully answers identity, platform classification, data-path discovery, and field assessment (title/start_date/end/venue_location/event_url all reach PROVEN directly from this one retained fetch). robots.txt imposes no crawl restriction. No CAPTCHA, login wall, or bot-challenge was encountered anywhere. Because Level 1 alone answered every question this investigation needed to resolve about acquisition technique, escalation to Level 2 (STRUCTURAL) or higher was not attempted — nothing observed suggested static inspection was insufficient. The one genuinely unresolved question (whether music can be mechanically isolated from the rest of the municipal cultural calendar) is a content-scope finding about the retained data itself, not a gap that browser/headless observation could resolve.

identity.notes: The retained homepage independently re-confirms official identity from its own content, not merely the task prompt's context note: <title>CM Maia</title>, a meta description reading 'Sítio oficial da Câmara Municipal da Maia. Informação sobre o município, composição e atividades. Inclui uma agenda de eventos no concelho.' ('Official site of Maia Municipal Council… Includes an events agenda for the municipality'), and og:site_name 'Câmara Municipal da Maia'. This matches the candidate's registry entry (official_website: https://www.cm-maia.pt, city/municipality: Maia) exactly.

site_classification.platform: Custom municipal CMS ('wm-smile'-branded front-end assets, WMCookieConsent consent script, wm:pagetype/wm:page_id meta tags) rendering fully server-side. Both the paginated event-listing pages and every individual event detail page contain their complete content in the initial HTTP response — no client-side rendering step is required anywhere. No JSON-LD schema.org markup and no RSS/ICS feed/alternate link were found on any retained page. Each event detail page instead embeds a structured (HTML var-tag based, not JSON) 'addtocalendar' widget carrying atc_date_start, atc_date_end, atc_timezone (always 'Europe/Lisbon' in the retained sample), atc_title, atc_description, atc_location, and atc_organizer directly — plus separately labelled Local:/Preço:/Organização:(/Horário: on some pages) fields that independently agree with the atc widget's own values. The listing page paginates via a simple query parameter (?events_list_54_page=N) with no authentication or token required.

title.notes: Every sampled event's title is stated directly and identically in at least three places on its own detail page (og:title, twitter:title, and the atc_title var), and matches the listing card's own <h2> text and aria-label verbatim. Mechanically confirmed for both of the 2 sampled events (Maia Blues Fest 2026, Sons de Verão 2026) in evidence/offline-proof-output.txt.

start_date.notes: The event detail page's own addtocalendar widget states atc_date_start directly as '2026-09-11 00:00:00' (a full, unambiguous ISO-style date with an explicit year) with atc_timezone 'Europe/Lisbon' — no combination of separate context fragments is needed, unlike the policy's DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT worked examples. This is independently cross-confirmed by a second, separate structured field on the same page (<meta name="content_date" content="2026-09-11T00:00:00.000Z">) and is consistent with the listing card's own '11 a 13 Set '26' day-range/2-digit-year text. The listing card's own 2-digit year ('26) is likewise a direct, unambiguous statement of 2026 in the source's own abbreviation convention, not an inference. Mechanically re-confirmed for both sampled events in evidence/offline-proof-output.txt.

time.notes: The addtocalendar widget's atc_date_start/atc_date_end are always stamped '00:00:00' — a day-level placeholder, not a genuine clock time. A separately labelled, genuinely structured 'Horário:' field exists and states a real time on some event pages (Sons de Verão: 'Horário: 18h30 e 21h30' — two performance times in one line), but is ABSENT on others (Maia Blues Fest, a multi-day, multi-act festival, where specific act times exist only inside unstructured 'Informação adicional' prose, e.g. '21h30 – Kenny "Blues Boss" Wayne', '17h00 – Maia Blues Fest Band'). Because this structured field is inconsistently present across the 2-sample set, and even when present is not always a single canonical event start time, time cannot honestly be marked PROVEN for a general collector.

end.notes: The same addtocalendar widget states atc_date_end directly ('2026-09-13 00:00:00' for the 3-day blues festival; '2026-09-06 00:00:00' for the 10-day 'Sons de Verão' series) — an explicit end date, not inferred from duration or guessed. Mechanically re-confirmed for both sampled events in evidence/offline-proof-output.txt.

source_record_id.notes: The event's own permalink URL, as directly self-declared by its own <meta name="canonical"> tag and matching the href used to reach it from the listing page, is used as source_record_id — the same policy-endorsed strategy already used by this project's own cm-gaia-eventos/paral-lel-62-barcelona-01 precedent (a permalink slug the source itself treats as its own canonical path). This investigation explicitly checked, and rejected, the two values that LOOK like structural ids on this platform: the page's own wm:page_id meta tag and the event_detail_<id> container id are both IDENTICAL ('3876' / '107') across the two genuinely distinct sampled events — proving neither is a per-event identifier at all, but a shared template/config id. This is exactly the trap this project's own stable-identifier rule warns about (the Hot Clube ICS UID precedent) — mechanically confirmed in evidence/offline-proof-output.txt, not merely asserted.

event_url.notes: Directly constructible and confirmed live: the listing page's own href for this event, and the detail page's own <meta name="canonical">, agree exactly. A plain GET of this URL returned HTTP 200 with the full event content server-rendered.

price.notes: Both sampled events carry a separately labelled 'Preço:' field stating 'Gratuito' (free admission) directly. This is honestly recorded as representative of the 2 sampled events, not a blanket claim that every event on this source is free — no paid-ticket example was encountered in this bounded sample, and that gap is noted rather than guessed at.

blockers.description: No dedicated, filterable music/concert category or tag exists anywhere in this source's own taxonomy. Across a bounded 5-page listing sample (60 events), the only category values observed are: Biblioteca, Cultura, Desporto, Desporto-Destaque, Educação, 'Homepage | Agenda - Eventos na Maia', Institucional, Juventude, 'Juventude | Homepage', Turismo — mechanically confirmed in evidence/offline-proof-output.txt. 'Cultura' is the closest bucket, but it bundles genuine music events (Maia Blues Fest, Sons de Verão) together with unrelated content under the same tag (e.g. 'Feira das Cebolas - Castelo da Maia' — an onion fair/market — is also tagged 'Cultura', observed on the same retained page). Unlike this project's cm-gaia-eventos precedent (an item-level 'música' tag that lets filtering stay mechanical and source-provided), this source provides no equivalently granular signal — isolating genuinely music-only events from the rest of 'Cultura' would require either title/description keyword matching (which this project's policy does not treat as mechanical, source-provided isolation) or a maintained editorial allowlist of known recurring series, which is an explicit human/operator scope decision this investigation is not positioned to make unilaterally.

The general listing (/agenda/todos-os-eventos) is a full historical archive, not a future-scoped feed: its last observed pagination page (283 of 283) contains events dated as far back as 2014 (mechanically confirmed in evidence/offline-proof-output.txt), and roughly 3,400 events are paginated across those 283 pages at 12 per page. Listing order is not strictly chronological page-to-page (page 1 contains a mix of near-term 2026 dates, not a clean ascending/descending sequence), so a future collector would need its own bounding logic to avoid importing over a decade of past civic events; this investigation did not attempt to design or prove that logic.

reasons: identity.status is PROVEN at HIGH confidence (the retained homepage's own <title>, meta description, and og:site_name self-identify as the official Câmara Municipal da Maia site), and site_classification.acquisition_class is STATIC_HTML — a resolved, supported class. The given sources/porto.json events_url turned out to be a stale, narrow single-weekend page (a 301 redirect target, not a usable feed), but this investigation independently discovered the site's own general listing root (/agenda/todos-os-eventos) exactly as this task anticipated, and confirmed it is a real, paginated, fully server-rendered event index.

Field extraction is genuinely strong for the two sampled music events: title, start_date, end, venue_location, event_url, and price are all PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE, each independently cross-checked against a second structured field on the same page (atc widget vs. meta content_date vs. labelled Local:/Preço: fields vs. the listing card). source_record_id is PROVEN using the event's own canonical permalink URL — this investigation also explicitly discovered and rejected a plausible-looking but genuinely unstable id (wm:page_id / event_detail_<id>, identical across two different events), the same class of trap this project's own stable-identifier rule already warns about.

The one genuinely unresolved gap is content scope, not acquisition technique: this source's own category taxonomy stops at a broad 'Cultura' bucket that mixes real, substantial, standalone music events (a 3-day international blues festival; a recurring outdoor concert series) together with unrelated cultural content (markets/fairs, exhibitions, and presumably theatre/talks not sampled here) under the same single tag — mechanically confirmed absent of any music-specific value across a bounded 5-page/60-event sample. Per this task's explicit instruction, a category/tag field is required for mechanical isolation, and AI/keyword title classification does not qualify as mechanical, source-provided isolation under this project's policy.

This is deliberately recorded as HUMAN_REVIEW rather than REJECT or READY_FOR_ACTIVATION: unlike wow-world-of-wine-gaia-01 (where music content was genuinely incidental, bundled only into dinner/hospitality packages within a non-events ticketing catalog), this source's music content is substantial and standalone, and the technical acquisition path is fully proven — so REJECT would understate a genuinely strong, working source. But forcing READY_FOR_ACTIVATION would require this investigation to unilaterally decide how 'real music events' get scoped out of a ~3,400-event general civic archive (e.g., a maintained allowlist of known recurring series vs. full 'Cultura'-category import with downstream filtering) — a deliberate editorial/collector-scope decision this policy reserves for an explicit human/operator call, exactly as hard-club-porto-01 reserved its own remaining year-handling gap for human review rather than guessing past it.

collector_assessment.blockers records this content-scope gap as MAJOR (not CRITICAL) precisely because it is a scope decision, not a technical/access blocker, plus a MINOR note that the listing root is a full ~12-year historical archive requiring its own future-only bounding logic that this investigation did not attempt to design.

evidence/offline-proof.mjs + evidence/offline-proof-output.txt provide a DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION evidence item: a dependency-free, no-network re-parse of every retained fixture that mechanically reproduces every claim above, including the identity check, the stale-lead-vs-general-listing contrast, the full category-taxonomy scan, the archive-scope (2014) check, and the wm:page_id/event_detail_<id> stable-identifier trap.

This decision is a research conclusion only — it does not edit sources/porto.json or any registry. A future re-investigation (e.g. after a human/operator decides the music-scope question) must be recorded as a NEW investigation citing supersedes: "forum-maia-01", never a rewrite of this record.
